overview: Black strikes at the centre at once. After 2.cxd5 Black recaptures with the queen (Qxd5, with Nc3 gaining a tempo) or the knight (2...Nf6 3.g3 Nxd5). White gets a small lead in development and a fianchetto, Black a solid position and the c-pawn exchange for a d-pawn. Play is quiet in the main lines, with the Icelandic-like gambits (Schulz, Löhn) rare.

white_ideas.idea: g3, Bg2 and Nc3 pressuring d5 and the long diagonal
Gain tempi on Black's queen with Nc3 and take space

black_ideas.idea: Recapture on d5 with the knight, play ...Nb6 and ...g6 or ...e5 and develop smoothly
Use the queen on a5/d6 with ...Nf6 and ...c6

typical_structures.structure: White d-pawn against Black c7/e-pawn, c-file half-open for White

character.notes: Main 2.cxd5 Nf6 3.g3 Nxd5 is quiet and sound.

gambit.notes: Main lines regain the pawn; Schulz and Löhn gambits are rare side lines.

approach.notes: A respectable reply played by strong players now and then; standard.

sublines_that_differ.name: Löhn Gambit
sublines_that_differ.how: Black offers a pawn for activity; rare.

character.reason: Quiet main lines, with a small edge for White.

structure.reason: Asymmetric pawns after cxd5, half-open c-file.

approach.reason: Strong players use it now and then, not offbeat.

plans.reason: White fianchettoes against the d5 knight or queen.
